items.title: LINK-HF2: AI wearable monitoring after HF discharge is feasible, but no reduction in rehospitalization in exploratory analysis (HFSA 2026, JACC: Heart Failure)
items.summary: In 171 patients discharged after acute heart failure, 90 days of AI-analysed continuous patch monitoring with clinician alerts reduced AI-detected physiological instability but did not significantly reduce HF rehospitalization in exploratory analyses (16.3% vs 18.7%; HR 0.90, p=0.76) or a composite of unplanned rehospitalization, ED visits and death.
bullets: Prospective randomized, open-label, blinded-endpoint feasibility trial at 5 Veterans Affairs medical centres (n=171; mean age 73, 7% women). All wore a multisensor patch for up to 90 days with AI analysis; alerts went to clinicians only in the intervention group (n=80 vs 91 standard care).

Median monitoring adherence was 72.4%; at least one alert was generated for 52.6% of patients, most often for elevated heart rate. Clinicians responded within a median of 1 day (range 1-5 days), most commonly by reassessing symptoms after 3 days (65.7%).

Exploratory endpoints: HF rehospitalization 16.3% vs 18.7% (HR 0.90, 95% CI 0.43-1.84; p=0.76); composite of all-cause unplanned rehospitalization, ED visits and mortality HR 1.03 (95% CI 0.63-1.70; p=0.89).
AI-detected physiological instability was lower with alerts (HR 0.76, 95% CI 0.60-0.97; p=0.025).

Take-home: detecting instability alone may not improve outcomes without clearly actionable signals and matching treatment responses. Presented at HFSA 2026 and published simultaneously in JACC: Heart Failure.
